The main takeaway from our work is that

Serratia spp. can be considered as a general elicitor of fungal stress response, which may have implications for the development of biological control strategies against R. solani and other soil-borne fungal pathogens.

R. solani responds to the presence of Serratia with an overall shift in gene expression, which includes the upregulation of genes involved in xenobiotic degradation and the downregulation of genes related to hyphal growth.
Serratia species are not only able to inhibit R. solani, but also to induce the expression of genes related to stress responses and to hyphal rearrangement.
